ledger.note: 1270: the Sambyeolcho rise. The Sambyeolcho page: 'rose in rebellion in 1270'; the Goryeo under Mongol rule page: 'the Three Patrols army (sambyeolcho) that served Goryeo's government rebelled against the Im family' and 'fled to Jindo Island and then Jeju Island'; the Mongol invasions page: 'resisted in the islands off the southern shore'. No page gives a month, a king or a capital.

ledger.note: 1271: the rebels hold Jeju. 'They fled to Jindo Island and then Jeju Island,' staying 'until 1273'; the move year is a bridge. Jeju was Tamna land, a vassal of Goryeo (tamna dossier).

region.text: Jeju Island, where the rebels 'stayed until 1273' (same page)

ledger.note: 1273: Goryeo crushes the rebels on Jeju. The Sambyeolcho page: the rebellion 'was crushed by the Korean-Mongolian alliance in 1273'; the Goryeo under Mongol rule page credits 'Goryeo forces' alone and adds that part of the island became 'a breeding ground for the Yuan royal herd'. No month on any page.

notes: Rebel state of three years, drawn as two island patches. The pages (Sambyeolcho, Mongol invasions of Korea, Goryeo under Mongol rule) name Jindo and Jeju and give no month, no king, no capital and no date for the Jindo-to-Jeju move; the pages opened give no date for the fall of Jindo and name no rebel king, so none are recorded. Gazetteer names needed: Jindo (island, 126.26E 34.48N, used as a coordinate radius). Cross-check: goryeo records Jeju (Tamna) as its vassal 938..1275 and defeating the Sambyeolcho in 1273; tamna should show the rebels on Jeju for 1271-1273. No Cliopatria row.
